```python
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("Transportation_Problem")
    m.setParam("TimeLimit", 100)  # Set time limit to 100 seconds

    # Data
    sources = list(range(4))  # S0..S3
    destinations = list(range(28))  # D0..D27

    supplies = [752, 850, 796, 766]
    demands = [47, 25, 32, 52, 15, 50, 62, 72, 38, 72, 69, 42, 34, 44, 48, 109, 52, 59, 54, 95, 91, 116, 47, 116, 24, 85, 32, 79]

    # Cost matrix: rows correspond to sources S0..S3, columns to destinations D0..D27
    costs = [
        [  8.04,  13.12,   9.65,  11.40,  17.60,  14.96,  10.01,  21.88,   6.64,   6.01,   5.35,  17.17,   5.57,  22.58,  21.15,  10.61,  18.17,  12.59,  11.85,   5.16,  24.61,  17.23,  29.17,  19.19,  16.93,  16.28,  13.89,  12.06],  # S0
        [ 23.27,  22.29,  10.91,  16.05,   7.31,  17.46,  11.38,  12.45,  25.86,   9.24,  14.42,  17.37,  13.05,   7.59,  27.59,  16.29,  22.67,  15.68,  26.62,  27.24,  29.73,  23.86,   5.79,  13.63,  26.30,  23.18,  15.08,  14.54],  # S1
        [  6.88,  13.86,  19.68,  25.29,  14.04,  15.26,  28.89,  26.22,  27.16,  16.66,  10.49,  15.42,   6.04,   9.48,  18.23,  19.01,  14.93,   7.01,  28.31,  19.94,  16.40,  11.43,   9.46,  12.22,   6.63,  28.37,  20.90,   9.43],  # S2
        [ 19.90,  20.54,  12.66,   6.16,  23.13,  18.53,   5.54,  21.68,  22.18,  22.10,  18.61,   5.99,  26.41,  27.00,  13.10,  29.36,  21.62,  12.24,  27.39,  17.87,  17.03,  16.95,  14.64,  23.81,  15.95,  17.05,  12.62,  16.10],  # S3
    ]

    # Decision variables:
    # Flow_S{i}_D{j} >= 0 is the quantity shipped from source i to destination j
    flows = {}
    for i in sources:
        for j in destinations:
            flows[(i, j)] = m.addVar(lb=0.0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=f"Flow_S{i}_D{j}")

    # Objective: Minimize total transportation cost
    m.setObjective(
        quicksum(costs[i][j] * flows[(i, j)] for i in sources for j in destinations),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # Supply constraints: Shipments from each source <= its supply
    for i in sources:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(flows[(i, j)] for j in destinations) <= supplies[i],
            name=f"Supply_S{i}"
        )

    # Demand constraints: Shipments to each destination >= its demand
    for j in destinations:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(flows[(i, j)] for i in sources) >= demands[j],
            name=f"Demand_D{j}"
        )

    m.optimize()
    return m
```

Subject: Shipping plan to reduce distribution costs and meet demand
Date: Today

Situation:
We operate a network with multiple sources supplying many destinations. To control transportation spend and protect customer service, we need a clear, feasible plan that aligns available inventory with destination requirements while using economical lanes. Shipments must be in whole units (no partial loads allowed), so load building and allocations must respect full-unit quantities.

Problem:
We need to determine how much to ship from each source to each destination so that no source exceeds its available inventory and every destination receives its required quantity. Shipping costs vary by route, and some pairings are significantly more expensive than others. The challenge is selecting routes and allocating whole-unit volumes in a way that covers all demand at the lowest total shipping cost.

Approach:
- Confirm available supply at each source and required quantities at each destination using the data in the annex.
- Review route-level shipping costs to understand relative lane economics.
- Develop a lane-by-lane allocation plan in whole units that keeps each source within its limits and fully covers destination needs.
- Validate operational practicality (appointments, carrier capacity, transit times) and adjust as needed without compromising demand coverage.
- Implement the plan, monitor execution, and proactively manage exceptions to avoid expedites and service failures.

Decision/Request:
Approval to proceed with this analysis and publish the recommended lane-level plan to operations. Upon approval, we will share allocations with sourcing, transportation, and store operations and begin execution in the next cycle.

To: Operations Leadership Team
From: Supply Chain Director
Date: 27 February 2026
Subject: Cost-effective shipping plan across our multi-source network

Situation
Our distribution network relies on multiple production and storage points to supply a broad set of downstream locations. Transportation spend is a major driver of delivered cost and a key lever for margin improvement. At the same time, reliable fulfillment underpins customer satisfaction and store readiness. We need a clear, cost-effective plan that aligns available inventory with destination needs while preserving service standards.

Problem
We must decide how much to ship from each source to each destination, given that each source has limited inventory and each destination has a required quantity. Shipping costs differ by route, and all shipments must be in whole units (no partial loads). The challenge is to direct flow along the lowest-cost routes without exceeding source availability and while fully meeting destination needs.

Goal
Create a shipment plan that:
- Meets every destination’s requirement in full
- Does not exceed available inventory at any source
- Uses whole-unit shipments only
- Achieves the lowest possible total transportation spend

Approach and next steps
- Validate the current supply at each source, required quantities at each destination, and lane-by-lane shipping costs (see Annex).
- Build a shipment allocation that uses only whole units and prioritizes the least expensive lanes while honoring inventory limits and complete fulfillment.
- Review operational practicality (lead times, carrier capacity, dock schedules) and minimize unnecessary source splits to simplify receiving where feasible.
- Deliverables will include recommended shipments by lane, confirmation that all orders are covered within available supply, and the resulting total transportation cost.
- Upon sign-off, transition the plan to transportation planning for tendering and execution, with weekly refreshes as inventory and demand change.
